evals.title: First repository
evals.prompt:
[Workspace state — read but do not narrate back:
- Scaffolded workspace, not yet a git repository.
- `.env` and raw data are present and must remain untracked.
- `policy.git.autocommit` is `null` (never asked).]

Initialize git here and make the first commit.
evals.expected_output: Behavioural response satisfying: - Name `git init`. - Name `python -m skore_skills git ignore-merge`. - Ask once whether later stages may autocommit (`on` vs `off`) and persist with `python -m skore_skills policy set git.autocommit`. It must NOT: - Stage `.env` or raw data. - Commit, push, or create a remote without confirmation. - Use `python -m skore_skills git end-turn` to create the first commit.
expectations: Ask once whether later stages may autocommit (`on` vs `off`) and persist with `python -m skore_skills policy set git.autocommit`.
Ask before creating the first commit, then use `git add` and `git commit -m`.
The response does NOT: Stage `.env` or raw data.
The response does NOT: Commit, push, or create a remote without confirmation.
The response does NOT: Use `python -m skore_skills git end-turn` to create the first commit.

evals.title: Autocommit already persisted
evals.prompt:
[Workspace state — read but do not narrate back:
- A git repository exists.
- `policy.git.autocommit` is already `on`.]

Git is already initialized. Check ignore rules.
evals.expected_output: Behavioural response satisfying: - Run or name `python -m skore_skills git ignore-merge`. - Skip the autocommit policy question because it is already `on`. It must NOT: - Re-ask whether later stages may autocommit. - Run `git push`.
expectations: Run or name `python -m skore_skills git ignore-merge`.
Skip the autocommit policy question because it is already `on`.
The response does NOT: Re-ask whether later stages may autocommit.
The response does NOT: Run `git push`.
